reason: Chapter 3 'Acetone' of `2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf` (ecoinvent report No. 8) is the dataset's own cited chapter. Its captioned inventory tables - Tab. 3.1 'Input data and functional unit outflow of the dataset for acetone production in Europe' (p.100), Tab. 3.2 (p.101) and Tab. 3.3 (p.102) - are deliberately NOT selected: they are the cumulated PlasticsEurope vector of this very dataset (resources and emissions plus waste-treatment services, no production input), i.e. the target's own answer, and sec. 3.6 says so outright: 'Due to the fact that this dataset is cumulated it was not possible to use the other processes modelled in econvent to obtain a transparent process chain.' The unit-process evidence is the uncaptioned text of sec. 3.5 on pp. 98-99, which states the route ('Acetone and phenol are co-products ... Both chemicals are produced primarily via the oxidation of cumene'), gives the two reaction equations with the cumene requirement - 'Wells (1999) indicates that 2300 kg of cumene are required to produce 1000 kg of acetone with a yield of 90%. The production of the co-product phenol is not included in this figure.' - and matches the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, 'production by oxidation of cumene'. Pages 100-102 are excluded from the range on purpose so that the target's own vector never enters the excerpt.
